sentences.text: This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail relating to Crime No.307/2024 registered at Police Station - Mahila Thana Padav, District - Gwalior (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 376, 354 and 506 of IPC.

Prosecution story in brief is that on 17.8.2024, prosecutrix submitted a written complaint at Mahila Thana Padav to the effect that she met applicant Deependra Pandey, Advocate in connection with a complaint registered by her at the police station which was registered at Crime No.53/2023 for offence under Sections 376, 376(2)(n) and 506/34 of IPC.

On 07.6.2023 at around 8:30 in the night,
he took the prosecutrix to his house and committed rape upon her.
He also pressurized the prosecutrix to marry him and sent NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:15698 2 MCRC-38000-2024 obscene messages and made video calls to the prosecutrix.
As per the allegations, thereafter, applicant again committed sexual assault upon the prosecutrix on multiple occasions.
Upon this complaint, present FIR has been lodged against the applicant.

Learned counsel for the applicant argued that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated which is evident from the fact that allegedly, the incident occurred with the prosecutrix, who is a major, educated woman, for the first time on 07.6.2023, however, the FIR has been lodged after a Deependra Kumar Pandey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95946528/
1 delay of one year and two months on 17.8.2024.

sentences.text: Since the FIR was lodged on the basis of the written complaint submitted by the prosecutrix, therefore, it cannot be said that the police has not recorded the version of the prosecutrix.
As per allegations made by the prosecutrix, after the incident of rape by the applicant / accused on 07.6.2023, she again met the applicant one day later who gave her the offer of marriage.
Thereafter, he started sending obscene videos and making video calls.

Thereafter,
on 27.6.2023, applicant / accused took the prosecutrix to a secluded place and sexually assaulted her.
Even after this incident, she never made any complaint or lodged any report.
It is highly improbable that even after being sexually assaulted by the applicant on various occasions, she kept meeting him alone.
It is also unbelievable that as per the allegations, first time, the incident occurred in the house of the applicant where he lives with his family members.
Since, applicant is already married, therefore, question of rape on the pretext of marriage also does not arise.

Learned counsel for the applicant further argued that despite having NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:15698 3 MCRC-38000-2024 sexually assaulted by the applicant, prosecutrix went with the applicant / accused to Aamkho in a room on 20.12.2023 where she was again sexually assaulted by the applicant.

As per the allegations, applicant came to Sahara Hospital on 02.7.2023 where she was getting treatment and, thereafter, she boarded the car of the applicant where she was again sexually assaulted by the applicant.

For an educated major woman who has already filed two rape cases against two different persons; one Dharmveer Bhadouria and another Mohit Garg bearing Crime Nos. 132/2021 and 53/2023 respectively, it is quite improbable that she would fall in the trap of the applicant / accused again and again.
Further argument is that a criminal case bearing Crime No.50/2023 for the offence under Sections 384 and 389 of IPC has also been registered against the prosecutrix for honey-trapping.

Present FIR is the counter-blast of the private complaint filed by the applicant against the prosecutrix for offence under Sections 296, 115(2), 333, 324,
305(A), 351(3), 61, 308(2), 308(7) of B.N.S in which learned JMFC took cognizance and the complaint was registered against her.

Learned counsel for the applicant further argued that the Rojnamcha Sanha No.23 dated 09.7.2024 of Police Station - University, District - Gwalior (M.P.) indicates that the prosecutrix threatened to commit suicide and created nuisance in the police station when wife of the applicant lodged a complaint against her which was informed to the senior police officers, however, despite the request,
she did not lodge any report against the applicant.

It is further argued that the prosecutrix has filed certain documents in defence to show the involvement of the applicant in the crime indicating NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:15698 4 MCRC-38000-2024 that some video-calls were made by the applicant to her, however, the video- calls are of before the alleged incident dated 07.6.2023.

Further argument is that custody of the applicant for collection of samples for FSL and DNA is not required in the light of the fact that allegedly, the incident occurred one year and two months back and, therefore, samples would have no significance.

Learned counsel for the applicant further argued that the allegation of the prosecutrix that her mobile phone was snatched by the applicant is an afterthought as it is not mentioned in the FIR which was registered on the basis of the written complaint submitted by the prosecutrix.
Applicant is a practicing advocate aged about 53 years.

He is practicing in the District Court, Gwalior for almost 27 years and is not having any criminal antecedents and there is no requirement of his Deependra Kumar Pandey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95946528/
2 custodial interrogations.

sentences.text: Prosecutrix is habitual of lodging false criminal complaints, which is evident from the fact that she has already lodged three FIRs. for sexual assault against different persons.
Criminal case of honey-trapping is also registered against the prosecutrix.
Under these grounds, he prayed for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the State as well as learned counsel for the prosecutrix vehemently opposed the bail application and argued that the prosecutrix has been victimized by the applicant / accused for a long period of time which is evident from her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. as well as other evidence and aplicant / accused is operating a gang to extort m o n e y f r o m p e o p l e b y t a k i n g u n d u e a d v a n t a g e o f N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2024:MPHC-GWL:15698 5 MCRC-38000-2024 his position.
Therefore, looking to the nature of allegations levelled against him as well as its gravity, applicant is not entitled for grant of anticipatory bail.
Hence, prayed to reject the application.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence available on record as well as in the light of the facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting upon the merits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to grant anticipatory bail.

Consequently, this application is allowed and it is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant be released on bail on executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer / Investigating Authority.

The applicant shall further abide by other conditions enumerated under Section 438 (2) of the Cr.P.C. and shall cooperate in the investigation, otherwise this bail order shall automatically stand cancelled.
Certified copy as per rules.
